subject: Spend sculpting: post-call recap & next asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@walletwave.com>; WalletWave Procurement <procurement@walletwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:05:12 -0800
Subject: Spend sculpting: post-call recap & next asks

Hi Sarah / WalletWave team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum:

Key pain points you shared
- Token spend spike on peak hours (recommendation traffic: highest 8% of requests account for ~45% of tokens).
- Latency sensitivity for checkout fraud-check path (95th pct target ~75–100ms).
- Procurement needs a tight TCO and a clear commitment path (pilot -> reserved sizing).

Goals we heard
- Proof-of-value pilot (6 weeks) to demonstrate 40–60% effective token cost reduction using batching + KV/prefix caching and a quantized model variant.
- Maintain output quality for fraud classification and reduce tail latency to <120ms for user-facing checks.
- Budget guardrail: pilot run-rate cap ~ $8k / month; ask to show scaling to production economics.

What Redwood will deliver (attachments included)
- walletwave_mvp_usage_estimate.xlsx — three traffic profiles (baseline, optimized-batching, optimized-cache+batch).
- mutual_action_plan.docx — proposed 6-week pilot milestones, success criteria, roles, and procurement steps.
- Short SOC2 + security summary link in the Drive (link below) for procurement review.

Open questions / asks for WalletWave
1) Can you confirm the 90-day and 30-day token volumes for the fraud-check endpoint (or share a small sample of anonymized request logs)?
2) Which SLA / procurement track do you prefer (standard monthly vs. reserved commit)?
3) Is Michael Lee the procurement lead we should loop for contract redlines and PO timing?

Suggested next steps
- Action: WalletWave sends 30-day token summary + confirm procurement contact (ideal by Wed 11/18).
- Action: Redwood to run a quick TCO sketch (attachment) and propose a one-hour procurement + security sync (Nov 23–24 window).

If that aligns, I’ll draft the MRP and a compact SOW skeleton to accelerate procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147
Redwood Inference

Attachments: walletwave_mvp_usage_estimate.xlsx (Excel, 42KB); mutual_action_plan.docx (Word, 28KB)

From: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@walletwave.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: WalletWave Procurement <procurement@walletwave.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:12:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Spend sculpting: post-call recap & next asks

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. That matches our notes. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Michael Lee (cc'd as michael.lee@walletwave.com) is our procurement lead; he will own the contract timeline and PO.
- CFO flagged that any pilot needs a clear path to a cost-per-transaction projection at production scale and an outline of discount thresholds tied to committed spend.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short data-flow diagram for the pilot (can be a redacted sample).

I'll share the 30-day token summary for the fraud-check endpoint by end of day Wed 11/18; Michael will confirm his availability for a procurement call next week.

Also, on latency: our engineering lead asked whether Redwood supports per-route prioritization to ensure fraud-check traffic stays on a low-latency path while background enrichment runs on cheaper lower-priority instances. Can you call that out in the TCO sketch?

Appreciate it — Sarah

Sarah Coleman
Head of Product, WalletWave
serious about keeping checkout fast

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@walletwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@walletwave.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:03:20 -0800
Subject: Re: Spend sculpting: post-call recap & next asks

Thanks Sarah — great context. Short replies inline and next actions below.

- Procurement / Michael: noted. I’ll add a commit-tier discount table to the TCO sketch showing 0%/10%/18% tiers at $0/$50k/$150k quarterly commitments. We can discuss custom thresholds on the procurement call.
- SOC2 & data-flow: shared the Drive link in the related links metadata — will also attach a one-page redacted flow in the DocuSign packet if that helps procurement.
- Per-route prioritization: yes — Redwood supports routing policies that pin specific routes to dedicated low-latency pools (we'll include latency delta and cost for that configuration in the TCO sketch).

Next concrete steps (what I’ll deliver by EOD Tue 11/17)
1) Updated walletwave_mvp_usage_estimate.xlsx: adds a per-route latency column and per-commit discount sensitivity.
2) Compact TCO one-pager that models three pilot scenarios (no-optimization, batching-only, batching+cache+route-priority) and the expected cost per 1M tokens.
3) Draft SOW skeleton & pilot checklist for Michael to review (DocuSign-ready).

Proposed meeting: Tue 11/23 at 10:00am PT for procurement + security + engineering. Michael, is that slot OK? If not, propose two alternatives.

On quoting your question about per-route prioritization, sample language we’ll include:

> Route-level priority pins fraud-check route to a dedicated low-latency GPU pool. Latency tradeoff: ~20–40ms improvement in P95 vs. mixed pools; cost uplift depends on utilization and can be offset with aggressive caching for other non-critical routes.

Looking forward — I’ll send the updated attachments shortly.

—Jonas

Attachments: (will attach updated walletwave_mvp_usage_estimate.xlsx and TCO_one_pager.pdf in follow-up)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:10:05 -0800
Subject: RE: Spend sculpting: post-call recap & next asks

Jonas / Grace — quick internal note before we send the SOW to WalletWave:

- Pricing suggestion: offer a pilot price cap at $8k/mo with an optional conversion credit of 50% of pilot overage applied to first month of committed contract if they convert within 45 days.
- Commit tiers to present: $0 (pay-as-you-go), $50k/qtr (10% discount), $150k/qtr (18% discount).
- Let's prefill the SOW with two options for route-priority: (A) shared pool + caching (lower cost), (B) dedicated priority pool (higher cost + SLA). Call out metrics we will measure: token burn delta, P95 latency, and modeled cost per 1M tokens.

If that works I’ll drop a SOW skeleton in the Drive and tag you both for final edits.

Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
